goldens.comment: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:537 — "cleaned annotations by time" success-path log uses Error level for a normal completed batch, same debug-leftover smell

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds success-path logging inside the new batched cleanup loop using `r.log.Error(...)`, e.g. `r.log.Error("cleaned annotations by time", "count", len(ids), "affected", x, "err", y)` (and similar for "Annotations to clean by time"). This will emit Error-level logs even when `y` is nil and the batch completed normally, which is an actionable operational concern (error log noise) but not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:554 — "Annotations to clean by count" logged at Error level for routine per-batch info

adjudication.rationale: In xorm_store.go the new batched cleanup logic logs routine per-batch state at Error level, e.g. `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by count", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, "cond", cond, "err", err)` (and similar "by time" and tag cleanup logs). These calls execute on every batch even when `err` is nil, so normal operation will emit Error logs (potentially very noisy and misleading). This is a real diff-grounded issue but not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:557 — "cleaned annotations by count" logged at Error level on the success path

adjudication.rationale: In the new batched cleanup logic for MaxCount, the success-path logs use `r.log.Error("cleaned annotations by count", ... , "err", y)` right after `x, y := r.deleteByIDs(...)` (with `y` expected to be nil on success). This will emit Error-level logs even when the operation succeeds, which is an operational concern (noisy/false error signaling) but not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:576 — "Tags to clean" logged at Error level for routine per-batch info in CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags

adjudication.rationale: In CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags, the new batched cleanup code logs routine per-batch state using `r.log.Error("Tags to clean", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, ...)` (and similarly `"cleaned tags"`) even when `err` is nil. This is not a functional correctness defect, but it is a concrete issue introduced by the diff because it will emit error-level logs during normal operation and may spam/trigger alerting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:579 — "cleaned tags" logged at Error level on the success path

adjudication.rationale: In CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags, the diff adds unconditional Error-level logs on the normal/success path: after fetching IDs it calls `r.log.Error("Tags to clean", ...)`, and after deletion it calls `r.log.Error("cleaned tags", "count", len(ids), "affected", x, "err", y)` regardless of whether `y` is nil. This is verifiable in the diff and can cause noisy/false error reporting, but it is not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:534 — Logged "err" value is always nil at this point since the preceding `if err != nil { return }` guarantees it, making the field misleading/dead

adjudication.rationale: In the new cleanup logic, after `ids, err := r.fetchIDs(...)`, the code immediately returns on `if err != nil { return 0, err }`. The subsequent `r.log.Error(..., "err", err)` lines (e.g., in the MaxAge and MaxCount batches) therefore log an `err` value that is always `nil`, making that field misleading/dead at that point. This is an observability/logging-quality issue introduced by the diff, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/annotations/annotationsimpl/xorm_store.go:536 — deleteByIDs's affected-row count is never compared against the number of IDs fetched, so the acknowledged TOCTOU window (rows deleted/changed by concurrent inserts between fetchIDs and deleteByIDs) can silently under-delete with no metric or reconciliation beyond a per-batch Error log line

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally introduces a fetchIDs → deleteByIDs two-step cleanup and explicitly notes it “may under-delete when concurrent inserts happen” (xorm_store.go CleanAnnotations). In deleteByIDs it returns RowsAffected, but callers only accumulate totals; there’s no check that `affected == len(ids)` or any explicit mismatch handling/metric—only logging of `count` vs `affected` via `r.log.Error(...)`. This is a real, diff-grounded observability/reconciliation concern, but not a correctness defect per se because the behavior is acknowledged and the loop retries on subsequent cycles.
